name: framer-multi-carousel

frames.best_why: Three complete photo cards with captions legible, before the row starts clipping at the edges.

tagline: Three captioned photo cards step sideways under round arrows.
summary: A row of image cards with a caption strip along the bottom, advanced one card at a time by overlay arrows. The visible count follows the window: one card on phones, three on desktops.
appearance: Three portrait photo cards stand shoulder to shoulder, each around 300px tall with softly rounded corners. A black fading band across the bottom of each card holds a small white caption. Two white chevron circles float over the middle of the left and right edges.
behaviour: Clicking an arrow slides the row by exactly one card with a spring, and the arrow dims to grey at either end of the set. Resizing the window changes how many cards fit, snapping the row back into range.
demo_content: Unsplash photos captioned MAXX PHAM and BOXIEN BAY: a sunglasses portrait, a sunlit green wall, blurred figures.
search_phrases: carousel showing three cards at once
multi slide photo gallery with captions
arrows to step through image cards
responsive image row one two three
photo cards with title gradient footer
horizontal image strip with round arrows
gallery that shows more slides on wide screens
use_when: Several images with short captions should sit side by side and the count should adapt to width.
avoid_when: Cards cannot be dragged, the row is fixed at 300px tall and captions never truncate.
customise: The breakpoints prop sets cards per width; photos, captions and the fixed card height are edited in the file.
weight_why: Eighteen images in a row, moved by a single spring transform on arrow clicks.

a11y.note: Arrows are icon-only with no accessible name, and alt text repeats the odd caption instead of describing the photo.

issues: Both arrow buttons are icon-only, so screen readers announce nothing useful.
The only heading is visually hidden, leaving the visible carousel unlabelled on the page.
polish_why: Even three-up layout with readable captions; the bare arrows are the only rough edge.
